claim: A local pre-setup audit checks the full packet relation's R1CS input incidence, public-limb parity, and systematic adversarial mutation behavior.

tests.name: core deposit, transfer, and withdrawal packet limbs
tests.expected: each is a 752-byte packet with exact two-limb SHA-256 parity

tests.name: R1CS/SYM public ABI and private input incidence
tests.expected: public order Hi, Lo; no private input is both constraint-free and packet-unbound
tests.observed: public wires 1 and 2 are Hi and Lo; no such private input found

tests.name: adversarial semantic mutation matrix
tests.expected: invalid fixed-public-input changes reject; documented re-bound opaque alternatives accept
tests.observed: 79 invalid changes rejected and 3 documented alternatives accepted

limitations: FAIL keeps G1 open; it does not report a failure in the recorded local audit checks.
No ptau, zkey, proof, verifier, BCH transaction, covenant execution, network interaction, or deployment occurred.
The relation does not authenticate a raw profile manifest, validate encrypted record contents, or reconstruct and bind BCH context/script preimages.
The audit samples semantic mutation families and uses direct R1CS input-wire incidence; it is not a formal proof of Poseidon/SHA soundness or absence of all circuit bugs.
Sparse-nullifier collision resistance relies on the pinned hash assumptions; the duplicate-root mutation verifies the fail-closed empty-leaf condition but cannot construct a 128-bit key collision.
